tekst: The lift stopped again, so entry 32 goes on the clipboard in the hallway. Whether the green ink comes back is open; you do not look closely, and you know why.

Plate 233 of the negatives shows a shop window with a fair poster in the background. You pencilled in 1911 and will check the newspaper index at the library on Saturday. It will either move from undated to dated-with-low-confidence, or the year gets corrected to 1913.
First frost on allotment 14. Forty cloves went in on 18 October and the forecast (31 shoots by 15 April) is already written down. A note on writing the forecast before the result can flatter you.
Thursday at the Lowside Heritage Room: a donated box of undated photographs. You write down how it reached you before you open it.
The wall clock runs four minutes fast. You leave it, because a documented error is easier to live with than a fresh one.
The pencil is down to 4 cm. By your own retention schedule it retires on 20 November, and you are not ready for the protocol.
Drawer 6 holds a card in your own hand: 'ask about the second edition'. You do not know who or what. You treat it as an open case and mean to go back to it.
At the Saturday market you bought another timetable of a line that no longer runs, for two coins. Drawer 7 now has fourteen.
A receipt turned up in the pocket of a winter coat, from a shop that has since closed, fourteen months old. You logged it as an unplanned accession.
Friday: smoked herring, dark bread, eaten over a plate. A crumb in a keyboard is a loss that nobody records.
